lean.fidelity_note: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and consider $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. There is a unique solution on that half-line, with $|Y|\le1$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$ for one function $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. Its amplitude $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$ equals $\sqrt{\cos\varphi}\exp\int_0^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$. It has its global maximum at the unique zero $\tau_m$ of $Y$, with $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, positive $Y$ before and negative $Y$ after, and $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)\ge\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. The formal statement therefore retains all the conclusions of Lemma 2.5. It makes uniqueness on $[0,\infty)$ explicit, matching the paper’s reference to “the solution,” and uses one common deviation $e$ in both representations. The equation, bounds and uniqueness concern only $\tau\ge0$, with a right derivative at zero; negative-time values are unrestricted. The statement does not assert that the perturbed amplitude has its maximum at the reference turning time.
